scope: Demonstrate the APK reproducibility mitigations identified by the root-cause pass: two independent clean rebuilds of :app:assembleStandardDebug with a fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, an explicitly pinned BUILD_ID and a clean app/build/app/.cxx (so packaging starts from scratch), then a byte comparison of the resulting debug APKs.
source_state: Both builds ran at git HEAD 50366b1b6672e0ee4ca64a98df49b1874a6390ad with a clean tracked working tree (the Lead's integration commit that also committed the root-cause deliverable predated build A). Build IDs are pinned explicitly so later docs/tool commits cannot change the result.

root_causes_to_mitigate: libcrypto.so differed only by the OpenSSL 1.1.1q build timestamp generated by util/mkbuildinf.pl, which honours SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH

classes16/23/30.dex differed only because the compared APKs had different git BUILD_ID values (BUILD_ID is emitted from `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD` unless overridden; app/build.gradle supports a Gradle property/environment override)
the 4.87 MB APK size delta and local entry order/padding differences came from incremental packaging hole/padding reuse, i.e. from packaging over a pre-existing APK instead of a clean app/build

fixed_inputs.SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH_semantics: the committer timestamp of the build commit (git log -1 --format=%ct 50366b1b) -> UTC 2026-10-21T23:27:14Z
fixed_inputs.BUILD_ID_mechanism: ./gradlew -PBUILD_ID=vapor-repro (app/build.gradle lines 179-182: Gradle property -> environment variable -> git short HEAD; the property wins)

rm -rf app/build app/.cxx (app/build 3.0G, app/.cxx 382M at removal; app/build/intermediates/cxx is inside app/build; deleting app/.cxx removes the CMake build tree, the native-network ExternalProject build tree and the generated OpenSSL crypto/buildinf.h, which forces OpenSSL's mkbuildinf.pl to regenerate the DATE string)

the Rust cargo target directory app/src/main/cpp/wn-steam-client/rust/target (503 MB) was intentionally NOT removed: it is unrelated to the three root causes, both builds ran with the same target state, and earlier evidence already showed libwnsteam.so is reproducible; this is recorded as a limitation

cause_classes: different git BUILD_ID -> three dex files
incremental packaging holes -> ZIP order/padding and 4.87 MB

mitigated.relation_to_previous: the mitigated APK hash intentionally differs from both previous APK hashes because it embeds BUILD_ID 'vapor-repro' (not 63a2bbb3/95ecbf62), a different fixed OpenSSL DATE, and a clean ZIP layout; the reproducibility claim here is build A == build B, not equality with those older artifacts

demonstrated: two independent clean builds of :app:assembleStandardDebug (each preceded by deletion of app/build and app/.cxx) with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792625234, -PBUILD_ID=vapor-repro, -PVERSION_CODE=1 and the Rust toolchain on PATH produce a byte-identical APK: sha256 f8cc0b2fd2bcf144d647e7d9e5695dec88b0822a1c23496af854bda77e3d7807, 676,228,770 bytes each, cmp-clean

the OpenSSL DATE string is the fixed epoch string 'built on: Wed Oct 21 23:27:14 2026 UTC' in both builds (and equals the expected gmtime(SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH)), including in the build that ran 7-16 minutes later, so mkbuildinf.pl used SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH rather than the wall clock
the dex files are byte-identical across the two builds with BUILD_ID 'vapor-repro' pinned (vapor-repro present, old commit-hash ids absent), and the D8 metadata/checksum map matched

clean app/build packaging removes the inter-entry holes/padding entirely: 0 bytes of inter-entry padding in both APKs vs 8,694,220/13,569,179 bytes in the previously compared builds; the APK is 8.7 MB / 13.6 MB smaller than those builds for that reason
all three root-cause predictions were confirmed in one experiment: the two previously differing native/dex entries are now identical and the previously differing ZIP layout is now identical and dense
what_else_is_needed: nothing further for reproducibility of this workflow on this machine: the two-run criterion is met

for a broader claim, the remaining gaps are cross-machine/cross-environment reproducibility (host paths, JDK/NDK/lld versions, OS), release-signing reproducibility (both tested APKs are Android-debug-signed), and a fully pristine-input run (this experiment intentionally kept the Rust cargo target dir and the Gradle dependency/daemon caches; a container/fresh-checkout run, or additionally wiping cargo target and Gradle caches, would be the stricter test)

for CI: set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to the commit timestamp and pass BUILD_ID explicitly (e.g. the release id), and clean app/build + app/.cxx before packaging; the same two-run byte comparison can then gate reproducibility

confirmed: Build A and build B APKs are byte-identical: same sha256 f8cc0b2f..., same 676,228,770 bytes, cmp reports no difference; the diff tool reports size delta 0, no differing entries, identical local entry order and 0 bytes of inter-entry padding.

Both builds deleted app/build and app/.cxx before compiling and both executed the CMake configure/build tasks (OpenSSL ExternalProject rebuilt from scratch); the Gradle task graph is the same (110 actionable / 47 executed / 63 up-to-date; 136 task log lines) with only parallel scheduling order differing.

The generated buildinf.h and the extracted APK libcrypto.so in both builds contain 'built on: Wed Oct 21 23:27:14 2026 UTC', equal to gmtime(SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792625234); build B's wall clock (23:34-23:43Z) differs from that string, proving the epoch was used.
The build-tree libcrypto.so (and its stripped APK entry) are byte-identical between build A and build B: build-tree sha256 c63f0446..., APK entry sha256 efbc6aa6....

The APK's BuildConfig.BUILD_ID is 'vapor-repro', classes23.dex is byte-identical between the builds (7e54c579...), the string 'vapor-repro' is present and the previous git-hash build ids absent in both.
The APKs verify with APK Signature Scheme v2 under the standard Android Debug certificate (cert sha256 7e122c92...) and pass zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4.
The APK is 8,697,866 bytes smaller than the root-cause source APK and 13,572,838 bytes smaller than the root-cause rebuild APK, matching the removal of inherited inter-entry holes/padding.
inferred: The mechanism connecting the fixes to the identical output is the root-cause model: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH removes the only libcrypto content difference and lld is deterministic for identical inputs (established separately in the root-cause report), pinned BUILD_ID removes the only dex content difference, and a clean app/build prevents packaging hole reuse. This experiment demonstrates the combined result; it did not isolate each mitigation with a separate control build (e.g. one build with only the epoch fixed), so the per-factor causal decomposition remains inferred from the root-cause evidence.
Byte-identical results on another machine, with a different JDK/NDK/lld, with a pristine cargo/Gradle cache, or with release signing are not established.
limitations: Two builds on one machine/workflow; cross-machine, cross-toolchain and release-signing reproducibility are out of scope.

Only app/build and app/.cxx were removed between builds; the Rust cargo target directory (503 MB) and Gradle caches were reused (they are unrelated to the three root causes and both builds saw the same state). A fully pristine-input test was not run.
Each build started from a clean tracked git tree at 50366b1b; app/ code was unchanged before and after the Lead's docs/tool commits, and BUILD_ID is pinned, so the result is not sensitive to HEAD.
The two APKs are Android-debug-signed with the standard debug certificate; the APK signing block contents are reproducible here only for that debug key.

No per-factor control builds (e.g. epoch-only or BUILD_ID-only) were run; the decomposition into three independent factors is inherited from the root-cause receipt and confirmed collectively by this experiment.
